payload.summary: The notebook-autoprune 'dropped-newest' signal emitter writes structurally invalid JSON, so its own warning signals can never be drained or routed.
payload.evidence: docs/signals/notebook-prune-dropped-newest-docs-agent-memory-notebooks-dev-mcp-server-md-2026-08-23T152548Z.json (1170B) fails JSON.parse at position 581: a bare '0,' token appears on its own line immediately after "sentinel_section_count": 0, indicating a lost field name / split value during serialization. drain-signals.js reports 'SKIP unparseable' and the file stays resident in docs/signals/ forever.
payload.why_it_matters: The signal's own stated purpose is 'this signal exists so the drop is never silent'. A malformed emitter makes the drop exactly silent: the autoprune proceeds, potentially dropping the NEWEST notebook section, and no consumer ever learns of it. Detection was written and then defeated by its own serializer.
payload.scope_note: Distinct from FIX-NOTEBOOK-AUTOPRUNE-ROLLING-SECTIONS-BYTE-COUNTED-BUT-UNDROPPABLE (the drop-ranking defect this signal was reporting, already tracked, occurrence 5). This row is about the emitter producing invalid JSON, not about which section gets dropped.
